Tuesday, September 15, 2026 Daily Digest

Gartner: AI Vendors Not Enterprise-Ready, Only 6% Embed AI in Workflows, Dreamforce 2026 Opens

Today's top stories in AI + enterprise tech

1

Gartner: AI Vendors Are Not Enterprise-Ready — "Trust Is Not Warranted"

At Gartner's IT Symposium, distinguished VP analysts Daryl Plummer and Kristin Moyer delivered a sharp rebuke of AI vendors: "Trust in these vendors is not warranted yet. They don't understand enterprise terms and conditions. They don't understand enterprise liability." Plummer cited the "out-of-control pace of innovation" where models have six-month lifespans with no legacy support — "that alone says they're not enterprise ready." Gartner research found 86% of CIOs see AI risks growing faster than value. The firm recommends establishing an "AI central bank" for governance, deploying "guardian agents" to kill rogue AI, and creating disaster recovery teams specifically for AI failures. Plummer's blunt warning: "If you are called to account and your answer is 'AI did it', you are in trouble."

2

Only 6% of Organizations Have Embedded AI in Workflows — The Ownership Gap Widens

Supermetrics CMO Andrea Linehan breaks down why AI adoption is stalling: only 6% have fully embedded AI in workflows, fewer than 11% have integrated marketing and data functions, and more than 60% cite the insight-to-action gap as a major holdup. Her practical litmus test: "If an insight surfaces on Monday morning, can the marketing team confidently change what is live in the campaign by Monday afternoon without opening a ticket and waiting three days?" On who owns AI in B2B marketing, Linehan argues activation must sit with marketing — otherwise you get "dashboards explaining what happened without giving marketers enough confidence to decide what to do next." The investment priority for most organizations: data foundation and integration, not more AI tools.

Read on Demand Gen Report →
3

Dreamforce 2026 Opens — Salesforce's AI Control Plane Goes Cross-Platform

Dreamforce 2026 kicks off today in San Francisco with Salesforce unveiling the "Enterprise AI Harness" — a unified control plane for data, identity, governance, and agents that extends beyond Salesforce apps via MCP, APIs, and plugins. The move brings Salesforce capabilities into Claude, Slack, Microsoft Teams, and other AI surfaces. Combined with last week's seven named Agentforce agents (Casey, Paige, Carter, Hunter, Marshall, Piper, and Fin), Salesforce is positioning itself as the enterprise coordination layer for multi-agent deployments. The company claims 7 billion agent actions delivered to date. The strategic shift: from CRM vendor to AI infrastructure provider.

Read on Salesforce →
4

Agentic AI Takes Over Digital Advertising — Archive Ships "Archie" for Creator Campaigns

The agentic AI wave hits advertising hard this month. Archive launched Archie, an AI agent purpose-built for creator marketing campaigns. Sabio partnered with Gentoro to deploy agentic AI in digital advertising execution. AutoBacklinks rolled out an AI agent for automated link-building. The numbers frame the shift: 88% of digital marketers now use AI tools daily (up from 73% in 2025), and AI spending hit 15.3% of marketing budgets according to CMO.Works. Gartner predicts 33% of enterprise software will include agentic AI by 2028, with 15% of daily work decisions made autonomously. The marketer's role is evolving from campaign operator to AI guide — less executing, more directing.

Read on Buildez →
5

Adobe Q3: CX Enterprise Coworker Attracts 1,700 Customers in First Quarter

Adobe's Q3 2026 earnings reveal strong traction for its agentic AI bet: CX Enterprise Coworker, the autonomous marketing workflow agent launched in June, has attracted over 1,700 customers and early adopters. The company posted $6.76B in revenue, with AI-first ARR up 150% and one billion users across consumer and business products. Adobe Experience Platform and apps saw ending ARR growth above 20%. At MAX 2026, Adobe will showcase "breakthrough innovations across Creative Cloud, new capabilities in Firefly, and connected workflows for Firefly Enterprise — all powered by Agentic AI." The bet: marketing organizations want autonomous agents that execute, not just tools that assist.

Read on Benzinga →

💡 My Take

The 6% number is the story. We're in the third year of the generative AI era, and only 6% of organizations have actually embedded AI into workflows. Not experimented with. Not piloted. Embedded. The Gartner critique hits the same nerve: vendors are shipping faster than enterprises can absorb, while enterprise buyers still lack the data foundations to make AI actionable. Dreamforce will showcase dazzling agent demos, but Andrea Linehan's question cuts through the noise — can you turn Monday's insight into Monday afternoon's campaign change? Most can't. The gap between AI hype and operational reality remains wide, which means the competitive advantage still goes to organizations that solve for integration, governance, and activation speed, not tool count.
